Codex review: blocked before merge. ## What this changes This PR expires disposable scratch after 24 hours and explains missing scratch files across artifact and Files transports. **Example:** An idle managed checkout contains .openclaw/tmp/proof/report.txt last modified 25 hours ago. - **Before:** The scratch file remains indefinitely. - **After:** Maintenance removes it, and its recorded artifact displays an expired-file explanation. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | Useful, coherently owned feature with meaningful supporting tests, but a confirmed platform defect and incomplete upgrade proof prevent readiness. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | Real behavior proof is not required for maintainer- or bot-authored pull requests. | | **Patch quality** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | 2 actionable review findings remain. | ## Product **Kind:** Feature · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** Disposable proof files and runtime coverage accumulate in long-lived checkouts, while deleted scratch references lack an understandable expiry state. **Reason:** The maintainer-authored direction provides bounded storage reclamation without another scheduler or configuration surface. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 3 items remain** Keep this PR open: the maintainer-approved cleanup feature is useful, but coverage cleanup fails for aliased macOS temp paths and expiry errors omit recovery guidance. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `a0f4a5fb1f1b88f09230cc3b6d549a436d58fe7d` ## Before merge - [ ] **Canonicalize the trusted runtime temp root before cleanup (P2)** - When os.tmpdir() returns /var/folders/... on macOS, fs-safe canonicalizes it to /private/var/folders/.... cleanScratch then rejects it because rootReal differs from path.resolve(target.root), so every coverage cleanup pass defers without removing expired directories. Canonicalize the trusted runtime temp root when constructing this target and retain symlink rejection inside it. This independently confirms the existing review comment. - [ ] **Give expired-file errors a recovery action (P3)** - Opening a cleaned report displays only “file expired (scratch cleaned after 24 h)”, leaving the user without a next action. The repository requires changed user messages to explain recovery. Keep the compact list label if desired, but make the opening/download error tell users to regenerate the file and save durable output outside scratch. - [ ] **Add data-model compatibility proof** - The review found that existing stored data may not work after upgrade. Show that existing data still loads and works with this change. ## Findings - [P2] Canonicalize the trusted runtime temp root before cleanup — `src/gateway/scratch-maintenance-custody.ts:248` - [P3] Give expired-file errors a recovery action — `src/shared/scratch-expiry.ts:2` ### Tests - Missing end-to-end proof: Supply a latest-stable upgrade run through real Gateway maintenance showing expired scratch removal, live/queued protection, durable-file preservation, and subsequent artifact access.
Agent review details ### How this fits together Gateway worktree maintenance combines registered checkout roots with current run and queue custody, removes eligible scratch through fs-safe, and exposes cleanup receipts and artifact availability to clients. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Hourly maintenance] --> B[Checkout inventory and run custody] B --> C[Bounded scratch cleanup] C --> D[Guarded filesystem removal] C --> E[Cleanup receipt] D --> F[Artifact and Files readers] F --> G[Expiry messages and HTTP 410] ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Retain the existing maintenance architecture, canonicalize the trusted runtime temp root, and provide actionable expiry errors. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? The macOS failure follows directly from passing an aliased os.tmpdir() path into the canonical-root equality check; no target code or tests were executed during this read-only review. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Reusing the maintenance scheduler, custody owners, guarded filesystem operations, and existing artifact transports is appropriate; the runtime-root admission needs a focused correction. Full review comments: - [P2] Canonicalize the trusted runtime temp root before cleanup — `src/gateway/scratch-maintenance-custody.ts:248` When os.tmpdir() returns /var/folders/... on macOS, fs-safe canonicalizes it to /private/var/folders/.... cleanScratch then rejects it because rootReal differs from path.resolve(target.root), so every coverage cleanup pass defers without removing expired directories. Canonicalize the trusted runtime temp root when constructing this target and retain symlink rejection inside it. This independently confirms the existing review comment. Confidence: 0.99 - [P3] Give expired-file errors a recovery action — `src/shared/scratch-expiry.ts:2` Opening a cleaned report displays only “file expired (scratch cleaned after 24 h)”, leaving the user without a next action. The repository requires changed user messages to explain recovery. Keep the compact list label if desired, but make the opening/download error tell users to regenerate the file and save durable output outside scratch. Confidence: 0.96 Overall correctness: patch is incorrect Overall confidence: 0.94 AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Codex review notes: model internal, reasoning medium; reviewed against [bf0d53d5c17a](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/bf0d53d5c17a666f34cfc3ef1671e726be235a9a). ### Provenance checked - `Background maintenance and removal admission` keeps the original intent (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192909: Prevent shared-storage removal bursts while retaining live-owner checks, cancellation, and shutdown drainage.) - `Artifact metadata and download projection` keeps the original intent (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158583: Prepare artifact downloads off the Gateway thread while retaining current authorization and excluding internal payload fields from public summaries.) - `Files download and missing-file responses` changes intended behavior with a stated reason (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172042: Provide connection-bound streaming downloads through existing session read permissions; this PR intentionally distinguishes missing scratch from ordinary missing files.) ### Testing Proof path: in-process harness. ### Security None. ### Evidence Acceptance criteria: - pnpm test src/infra/scratch-cleanup.test.ts src/gateway/scratch-maintenance-custody.test.ts - pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/artifacts.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.test.ts src/gateway/control-ui-assistant-media-metadata.test.ts src/gateway/control-ui-assistant-media-policy.test.ts - pnpm check:changed - git diff --check What I checked: - **Reviewed introduction and current main:** The introduced patch adds scratch cleanup to the existing maintenance owner; fetched main retains worktree and workspace maintenance without this scratch pass. ([`src/gateway/worktree-maintenance.ts:280`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a0f4a5fb1f1b88f09230cc3b6d549a436d58fe7d/src/gateway/worktree-maintenance.ts#L280), [a0f4a5fb1f1b](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/a0f4a5fb1f1b88f09230cc3b6d549a436d58fe7d)) - **Aliased runtime root is rejected:** The coverage target passes os.tmpdir() unchanged, while cleanScratch refuses roots whose canonical path differs from their resolved spelling; this confirms the concern in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193677#discussion_r4484742589. ([`src/gateway/scratch-maintenance-custody.ts:248`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a0f4a5fb1f1b88f09230cc3b6d549a436d58fe7d/src/gateway/scratch-maintenance-custody.ts#L248), [a0f4a5fb1f1b](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/a0f4a5fb1f1b88f09230cc3b6d549a436d58fe7d)) - **Pinned dependency contract:** The patch imports @openclaw/fs-safe/root, pinned to 0.27.1 by the target package manifest; that release computes rootReal with realpathSync.native, establishing the canonicalization behavior and making its filesystem-boundary policy applicable. ([`src/root-context.ts:99`](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/blob/ea225ba262cf4ab86edc12abe374dfc9068833ff/src/root-context.ts#L99), [ea225ba262cf](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/commit/ea225ba262cf4ab86edc12abe374dfc9068833ff)) - **Supplied screenshots inspected:** The three linked scratch screenshots show the report row before expiry, its expired title, and the opening error; their committed browser scenario supplies these responses through installMockGateway. ([`ui/src/e2e/chat-workspace-files.e2e.test.ts:31`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a0f4a5fb1f1b88f09230cc3b6d549a436d58fe7d/ui/src/e2e/chat-workspace-files.e2e.test.ts#L31), [a0f4a5fb1f1b](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/a0f4a5fb1f1b88f09230cc3b6d549a436d58fe7d)) - **Accepted retention direction:** The maintainer-authored PR explicitly selects fixed 24-hour disposal, preserves live and queued checkouts, and excludes idle sessions and artifact references from retention protection; this direction requires no additional product approval. Public docs: [`docs/concepts/managed-worktrees.md`](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/managed-worktrees). ([`docs/concepts/managed-worktrees.md:585`](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/managed-worktrees), [a0f4a5fb1f1b](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/a0f4a5fb1f1b88f09230cc3b6d549a436d58fe7d)) - **Feature history and preserved pacing:** History identifies Peter Steinberger as the background-GC implementer and subsequent maintenance contributor; https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192909 explains the existing storage-pressure pacing, which this PR retains. ([`src/gateway/worktree-maintenance.ts:243`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/bf0d53d5c17a666f34cfc3ef1671e726be235a9a/src/gateway/worktree-maintenance.ts#L243), [bf0d53d5c17a](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/bf0d53d5c17a666f34cfc3ef1671e726be235a9a)) ### PR surface Source +707, Tests +605, Docs +2, Other +232.
